questions.stem: This peripheral blood smear shows an increased number of the arrowed cells, all with normal nuclear segmentation of 2 to 5 lobes. What is the most common underlying cause of this finding?

explanation.summary: The cells are mature segmented neutrophils, consistent with benign mature neutrophilia. This most commonly occurs as a reactive response to bacterial infection or inflammation (also stress, smoking, and corticosteroids).
explanation.whyCorrect: The cells are mature segmented neutrophils, consistent with benign mature neutrophilia. This most commonly occurs as a reactive response to bacterial infection or inflammation (also stress, smoking, and corticosteroids).

questions.stem: The neutrophil at the center of this smear contains prominent dark primary granules that stain nearly the same color as its nucleus. What does this toxic change most commonly indicate?

explanation.summary: This is toxic granulation, an increase in darkly staining primary granules. It is a toxic change seen with bacterial infections and inflammation, reflecting activated neutrophil production.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is toxic granulation, an increase in darkly staining primary granules. It is a toxic change seen with bacterial infections and inflammation, reflecting activated neutrophil production.

questions.stem: This neutrophil shows small clear bubbles in its cytoplasm in addition to coarse toxic granules. What process produces these vacuoles?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Degranulation of lysosomes during phagocytosis, typically in sepsis

explanation.summary: Cytoplasmic vacuolization results from degranulation of lysosomes within neutrophils, usually during widespread destruction of pathogens. It is most often seen in sepsis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cytoplasmic vacuolization results from degranulation of lysosomes within neutrophils, usually during widespread destruction of pathogens. It is most often seen in sepsis.

questions.stem: The arrow points to a small pale blue-gray inclusion at the periphery of this neutrophil's cytoplasm. What is this structure composed of?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ribosomes and remnants of rough endoplasmic reticulum

explanation.summary: This is a Dohle body, a peripheral blue-gray cytoplasmic inclusion made of ribosomes and remnants of rough endoplasmic reticulum. It reflects increased protein production in neutrophils responding to bacterial infection.
explanation.whyCorrect: This is a Dohle body, a peripheral blue-gray cytoplasmic inclusion made of ribosomes and remnants of rough endoplasmic reticulum. It reflects increased protein production in neutrophils responding to bacterial infection.

questions.stem: This figure compares lymphocyte morphology: cell A appears small and normal, while cells B and C are larger, with more abundant and irregular cytoplasm. What term best describes cells B and C?

explanation.summary: Cells B and C show the enlarged, voluminous, sometimes deeply basophilic cytoplasm of reactive lymphocytes, typically seen in viral infections, as opposed to the small mature lymphocyte in A.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cells B and C show the enlarged, voluminous, sometimes deeply basophilic cytoplasm of reactive lymphocytes, typically seen in viral infections, as opposed to the small mature lymphocyte in A.

questions.stem: This smear shows enlarged lymphocytes with abundant, deeply basophilic cytoplasm that molds around neighboring red cells. This reactive appearance is most characteristic of which category of illness?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Viral infection such as infectious mononucleosis

explanation.summary: These are reactive lymphocytes, larger than normal with voluminous, deeply basophilic cytoplasm. They are classically produced by viral infections, especially infectious mononucleosis (EBV).
explanation.whyCorrect: These are reactive lymphocytes, larger than normal with voluminous, deeply basophilic cytoplasm. They are classically produced by viral infections, especially infectious mononucleosis (EBV).

questions.stem: This large lymphocyte has abundant pale cytoplasm that abuts and molds around the adjacent red blood cells, giving a 'fried egg' appearance. It is most classically associated with which virus?

explanation.summary: This is a Downey type II cell, a reactive lymphocyte with abundant agranular cytoplasm that molds around neighboring erythrocytes. It is the most common reactive lymphocyte and is classically associated with Epstein-Barr virus (infectious mononucleosis).
explanation.whyCorrect: This is a Downey type II cell, a reactive lymphocyte with abundant agranular cytoplasm that molds around neighboring erythrocytes. It is the most common reactive lymphocyte and is classically associated with Epstein-Barr virus (infectious mononucleosis).
